issues.legal_issue: A stranger to a possession decree who claims an independent interest in the property and resists execution before being dispossessed may have that claim adjudicated before delivery of possession.
material_facts: A possession decree had been made against a judgment-debtor, and execution was commenced to deliver the property to the decree-holder.
A person who was not a party to the decree claimed an independent interest in the property and resisted the bailiff’s attempt to execute the warrant.
Before actual delivery of possession, the objector asked the executing court to decide his objections, but the court rejected the request solely because he had not yet been dispossessed.
issues.conclusion: The objector was entitled to have his claim adjudicated before delivery of possession; he was not required to wait until dispossession and then apply for restoration.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rules 97, 98, 99 and 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure establish procedures for adjudicating resistance before dispossession and claims for restoration after dispossession. Rule 97 applies when execution is resisted; Rule 99 applies when a person other than the judgment-debtor has already been dispossessed. The executing court must adjudicate relevant questions of right, title or interest, and refusing to hear a timely objector would also offend natural justice. The Court relied on Bhanwar Lal v. Satyanarain and Another, which recognized that a person resisting execution may raise an independent claim under Rule 97.

rule.if: possession_decree_execution and stranger_claims_independent_interest and stranger_resists_execution and stranger_seeks_adjudication_before_dispossession

predicates.possession_decree_execution: A decree-holder is seeking to obtain possession of immovable property through execution of a possession decree.
predicates.stranger_claims_independent_interest: A person who is not bound by the decree claims an interest in the property independent of the judgment-debtor.
predicates.stranger_resists_execution: That person resists or obstructs the attempt to execute the possession decree.
predicates.stranger_seeks_adjudication_before_dispo: That person asks the executing court to decide the claim before being dispossessed.
predicates.independent_claim_adjudicated_before_del: The executing court decides the stranger’s claim before delivering possession under the decree.

issues.definition: When a person outside a possession decree claims an independent interest, resists execution, and seeks a decision before dispossession, the claim must be decided before possession is delivered.

issues.legal_issue: When a decree-holder seeks police-assisted re-execution after a stranger has obstructed delivery of possession, the request is in substance an application to remove the obstruction and must be adjudicated as such.
material_facts: The bailiff reported that the attempt to execute the possession warrant had been resisted and obstructed by persons including the objector.
After learning of the obstruction, the decree-holder sought a fresh warrant for possession with police assistance.
The executing court did not adjudicate the obstruction or the objector’s claim and instead treated the objector’s request for adjudication as premature.
issues.conclusion: The decree-holder’s application for a fresh warrant with police assistance had to be treated as an application to remove the obstruction and adjudicated after hearing the decree-holder and the objector.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rule 97(1) permits a decree-holder who is resisted or obstructed in obtaining possession to apply to the executing court, and Rule 97(2), read with Rules 98 and 101, requires adjudication of the dispute. Order XXI Rule 35 permits delivery of possession and removal of persons bound by the decree, but cannot be used to bypass the procedure for dealing with a stranger’s obstruction. Under Bhanwar Lal v. Satyanarain and Another, the court must consider the substance of an application and may treat a request ostensibly made under Rule 35 as an application under Rule 97 when it seeks removal of an obstruction.

predicates.possession_decree_execution: A decree-holder is seeking to obtain possession of immovable property through execution of a possession decree.
predicates.stranger_obstruction_known: The decree-holder and executing court know that a person outside the decree has obstructed delivery of possession.
predicates.decree_holder_seeks_police_assisted_reex: The decree-holder seeks a fresh or renewed attempt to deliver possession with police assistance.
predicates.request_treated_as_obstruction_applicati: The request is treated as an application to remove the obstruction and is adjudicated after hearing the affected parties.

issues.definition: When an obstruction by a stranger is known and the decree-holder seeks police-assisted re-execution, the request is treated as one requiring adjudication of the obstruction.
